title: Flow cytometry detection of surface and intracellular antigens in pancreas from a single mouse embryo
protocol: Thaw FBS in a water bath.
Add 1 mL FBS to 9 mL DMEM/F12 medium in a sterile 15 mL tube and gently mix by inverting the tube.
Store the prepared DMEM/F12 medium with 10% FBS at 4°C for use within one week.
Thaw one vial of 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA at 20°C–22°C.
Add 0.5 mL 0.25% Trypsin-EDTA to 9.5 mL PBS w EDTA in a 15 mL tube.
Store the prepared trypsin solution at 4°C for use within one week.
Thaw 3 vials of FBS in a water bath.
Add 100 mL of FBS to 900 mL of sterile PBS.
Store the prepared FBS/PBS solution at 4°C for use within two weeks.
Take 497.5 mL FBS/PBS from step and add 2.5 mL Tween-20.
Store the prepared FBS/PBS with 0.5% Tween-20 solution at 4°C for use within two weeks.
Thaw one vial of 2% formaldehyde (100 μL needed per sample).
Store the thawed formaldehyde on wet ice for fixation.
Prepare a stereoscope laboratory station with a wet-ice bucket, two dissection forceps, and ice-cold sterile 1× PBS.
Place 1.5 mL Eppendorf tubes containing 500 μL DMEM medium on wet ice.
Euthanize the pregnant female by cervical dislocation.
Isolate the uterus containing embryos from the pregnant female.
Move the uterus with embryos to ice-cold sterile 1× PBS in a Petri dish stored on wet ice.
Dissect embryos one by one from the uterus and move them to a small clean Petri dish containing ice-cold sterile 1× PBS.
Assign embryos ID numbers starting from 1.
Check for fluorescence under a stereoscope equipped for fluorescence imaging.
Note down the ID number of fluorescent positive and negative embryos.
Dissect the organ of interest from the embryos using two #1 Dumont forceps.
Dissect the four paws from each embryo.
Transfer one paw from each embryo to a PCR tube on wet ice (optional).
Move the dissected organ of interest and one paw or all remaining paws into ice-cold 500 μL DMEM in Eppendorf tubes on wet ice.
Digest tissue with Liberase TM in DMEM by adding 1.25 μL Liberase TM (22.6 mg/mL).
Add 4 μL DNAse I (10U/μL) to the digested tissue sample.
Incubate at 37°C, 20 min, at 950 rpm on a thermomixer.
Triturate gently every 3–4 min using a P1000 pipette.
Centrifuge tubes at 500 g for 4 min at 4°C and carefully aspirate and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend digested tissue in 100 μL of 0.0125% Trypsin-EDTA with 4 μL DNAse I (10U/μL) added.
Incubate 37°C for 10 min, at 950 rpm on a thermomixer.
Triturate gently every 3-4 minutes using a P1000 pipette.
Change tips between samples.
Check that tissue has completely disintegrated.
Spin the sample down.
Resuspend pellet with 1000 μL ice-cold 10% FBS in DMEM to inactivate trypsin.
Filter cells into Eppendorf tubes using single-use cell strainers to make a single-cell suspension.
Wash the strainer with 500 μL FBS/PBS into the tube.
Carefully handle cells during washing steps to avoid losing them.
Keep all reagents on wet-ice.
Include 10% FBS in all steps below, except for Ghostdye staining and fixation, to block unspecific protein binding during staining and keep cells dissociated and alive before fixation.
Remove supernatant and resuspend in 1000 μL pure sterile PBS.
Spin cells down and remove the supernatant.
Resuspend in 1000 μL pure sterile PBS.
Spin Ghostdye only control and samples.
Set aside remaining controls not stained with Ghostdye on wet ice during steps e-i.
Prepare 100 μL of dPBS with a 1:1000 dilution of Ghost dye (Ghost dye Red-780) per sample.
Resuspend cells in the Ghost dye solution.
Mix immediately.
Incubate for 30 min at 4°C protected from light.
Spin all samples and controls.
Resuspend in 1000 μL FBS/PBS.
Spin.
Resuspend in 1000 μL FBS/PBS.
Stain with primary antibody for extracellular antigen.
Set aside controls which do not require staining with the primary antibody for extracellular antigen in FBS/PBS on wet ice.
Prepare enough primary antibody dilution to stain all samples, allowing 100 μL per sample and adding at least 10% extra volume.
Prepare primary antibody dilution in FBS/PBS.
Spin samples and controls requiring staining with the primary antibody for extracellular antigen.
Resuspend cells in 100 μL diluted primary antibody per sample.
Incubate for 30 minutes rotating at 4°C protected from light.
Add 1000 μL ice-cold 10% FBS/PBS.
Spin all samples and controls.
Resuspend in 1000 μL ice-cold pure sterile PBS.
Fix cells by resuspending in 100 μL 2% PFA for 15 minutes at 20°C–22°C protected from light.
Add 1000 μL ice-cold pure sterile PBS.
Spin samples.
Resuspend in 1000 μL ice-cold FBS/PBS.
Stain with primary antibody for intracellular antigen.
Prepare enough primary antibody dilution to stain all samples in 100 μL FBS/PBS with 0.5% Tween20 per sample.
Mix gently and add 1 μL antibody in 999 μL FBS/PBS with 0.5% Tween20 for a total of 1 mL.
Resuspend cells from samples requiring primary antibody for intracellular antigen in 100 μL diluted primary antibody per sample.
All other controls are resuspended in 100 μL FBS/PBS with 0.5% Tween20.
Incubate for 30 min rotating at 4°C protected from light.
Add 1000 μL FBS/PBS with 0.5% Tween20.
Spin to resuspend in 1000 μL FBS/PBS.
Repeat this wash at least once.
Stain with secondary antibody for unconjugated primary antibodies.
Incubate all samples and controls for 10 min rotating at 4°C protected from light.
Add 1000 μL FBS/PBS and spin.
Repeat the wash at least twice.
Resuspend cells in 100 μL of diluted secondary antibody per sample if intracellular antigen staining is required.
For other samples, resuspend in 100 μL FBS/PBS with 0.5% Tween20.
Prepare samples for flow analysis by resuspending in 100 μL ice-cold 10% FBS/PBS.
Immediately analyze samples using flow cytometry.
Analyze samples immediately to prevent loss of fluorescence intensity.
Gate cells based on their light-scattering properties using flow cytometry.
Gated cells are further classified by their fluorescent intensities from endogenous fluorescence and immunofluorescent staining.
Prepare and calibrate the flow cytometer according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Startup system and select appropriate laser lines and filters.
Perform fluidics start-up and de-bubbling.
Calibrate laser delays.
If sorting, calibrate drop delay and side streams.
Setup experiment or load previous settings.
Acquire and save single fluorophore/fluorescent protein controls for compensation to correct for spectra overlap.
Use single-fluorophore/fluorescent protein controls to perform compensation according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Set gates for your fluorophores based on the controls.
Use the no fluorophore control to set gate 1 on the FSC-A vs SSC-A plot to remove debris.
Use the no fluorophore control to set gate 2 on the FSC-W vs FSC-H plot to remove doublets.
Use the Ghost dye only control to set gate 3 and remove dead cells.
Use the no fluorophore control, the secondary antibody only control, and single-fluorophore/fluorescent protein controls to set gate 4.
Ensure that the no fluorophore control has no positive cells in gate 4.
Ensure that the secondary antibody only control has no positive cells in gate 4.
Record the samples one at a time.
Record all events in each sample.
